You are a CODE CLEANUP reviewer focused on ONE angle: EFFICIENCY. Do not hunt for correctness bugs.

The diff under review is at: /tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/9fb5c597-ba1e-4046-8ada-d69e84b4f335/scratchpad/simplify_diff.txt

It adds Andes V5 CSR transport across 3 repos:
- andesim_abi (ABI header): /home/nick/work/andesim/include/hybrid/state_abi.h , state_abi_check.h
- andesim (driver+plugin): /home/nick/work/andesim/driver/state_diff.cpp , driver/state_diff_test.cpp , qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c
- hybrid_vsim: /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp , state_drain.hpp , and tests/hybrid/*.test.cpp

YOUR TASK: Flag wasted work the diff introduces. Candidates:
- `andes_verify_excluded` in state_diff.cpp allocates a std::string per comparison (`std::string(name) == "msp_bound" || std::string(name) == "msp_base"`) — two heap-capable string constructions per field, per diff call. Cheaper alternative? (this is on the verify path, called once per run, so weigh whether it matters.)
- Any redundant re-computation inside the X-macro loops (e.g. recomputing an index/address that could be hoisted).
- hybrid_handoff.c resolve_handles: is `find_reg` (a linear scan of the gdb register list) called once per Andes CSR — is that the same cost model as the existing pmpcfg/pmpaddr resolution, or worse?
- Repeated I/O on the DMI bus: the restore/drain loops issue one DMI transaction per CSR. Is any of it avoidable or batchable given how the existing code does it? (Probably inherent — note if so.)
- Any long-lived object built from a closure/captured environment.

Be pragmatic: most of this is cold-path setup/verify code run once per handoff, NOT a hot loop. Explicitly rank each finding by whether it is on a hot path or a once-per-run path. Read the actual files to confirm. For each finding give: file, line, one-line summary, the cheaper alternative, and the concrete cost. If the only findings are trivial cold-path micro-optimizations, say so plainly. Return a concise bulleted list.

I have read all the relevant code across the three repos. Here is my efficiency review.

## Efficiency review: Andes V5 CSR transport diff

Bottom line: every code path this diff touches is once-per-handoff setup/verify/drain. There are no hot-loop regressions. One legitimate micro-opt exists; the rest is inherent to the DM abstract-command model or consistent with pre-existing patterns.

### Findings (all COLD / once-per-run)

- **`andes_verify_excluded` builds `std::string` to compare literals** -- `/home/nick/work/andesim/driver/state_diff.cpp:92-97`. Up to 2 `std::string` temporaries per scalar field (x13 fields ~= 26 constructions), plus `cmp(r, name, ...)` promotes the `const char*` literal to a 3rd `std::string` per field (its param is `const std::string&`). Cheaper: `std::strcmp(name,"msp_bound")==0 || std::strcmp(name,"msp_base")==0`. Concrete cost: in practice ZERO heap allocations -- every Andes name is <=14 chars and fits libstdc++'s 15-byte SSO, so this is just ~26 strlen+SSO-copies, sub-microsecond, on the `--verify` path called once per run. Real but immaterial; do it for cleanliness, not speed.

- **`resolve_handles` does 31 extra linear `find_reg` scans** -- `/home/nick/work/andesim/qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:162-173`. Each `find_reg` is an O(R) scan of the gdb register list with `g_ascii_strcasecmp` (R ~= 150). The diff adds 13 scalar + 2 pmacfg + 16 pmaaddr = 31 lookups (+18 `g_snprintf`). This is the SAME cost model as the existing pmpcfg(16)+pmpaddr(64)=80 scans right below it, not worse per call. `resolve_handles` runs once per drain, and the drain trigger fires once before `exit(200)`, so it is strictly once-per-process. A name->handle hash map would make the whole function O(R) instead of O(N*R), but that is a pre-existing design choice the diff faithfully follows -- not a regression. Inherent.

- **One DMI transaction per CSR in resume/drain** -- restore `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp:252-263`, drain `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp:115-125`. Resume adds 31 `write_csr_tolerant` (each ~= data0+data1+command writes + cmderr read = ~4-5 DMI ops); drain adds 31 `read_register_64`. Not batchable: the RISC-V Debug Module abstract-command interface is one-register-per-command, and the existing code already issues one transaction per GPR/FPR/pmpaddr (64 of those). Matches the established pattern; once per handoff. Inherent.

- **`"pmacfg"/"pmaaddr" + std::to_string(i)` per PMA field** -- `/home/nick/work/andesim/driver/state_diff.cpp:100-105`. 18 heap-allocating string builds. Identical to the pre-existing `"x"+to_string(i)`, `"v"+to_string(i)`, `"f"+to_string(i)` loops in the same function; `cmp` takes `const std::string&` so the string must materialize. Consistent, once per run. Not a regression.

- **No long-lived closure object** -- the `andes_verify_excluded` lambda captures nothing (`[]`), is stack-local, and dies with `diff_states`. Nothing to flag here.

- **X-macro loops have no hoistable recomputation** -- the scalar restore/drain/diff macros use compile-time constant `addr`; the PMA loops compute `HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR + i` / `HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR + 2*i`, trivial integer adds that cannot be hoisted. `regno_csr()` is identity (`return csr`). Clean.

### Verdict
The only finding with a concrete cheaper alternative is the `std::string`->`strcmp` swap in `andes_verify_excluded`, and even that costs nothing measurable (SSO, no heap, once per `--verify`). Everything else is either inherent to the Debug Module model or a faithful copy of the existing pmp/GPR/V cost model. No hot-path waste introduced.
